manifest.title: The equational theory of rational string-to-string functions

inputs.abstract:
A formalisation of the paper *The equational theory of rational string-to-string functions*
by Mikołaj Bojańczyk, Kacper Lewandowski and Katzper Michno.

Rational string-to-string functions are presented by a compositional syntax of *rational
terms* $f : A \to B$ between types built from $1$, $\times$, $+$ and lists $A^*$: a finite
set of atomic functions closed under composition and the functoriality combinators. The
paper gives a finite, purely equational axiomatisation of these terms (sixteen uniform
families of axioms and no implication rules), and its main result is that it is sound and
complete: two rational terms have the same denotation if and only if they are provably
equivalent (Theorem 4.1).

The submission states the definitions and results of the main part of the paper and proves
all of them, except Theorem 3.2 (every rational function is defined by a rational term),
which is recorded as an open statement and on which nothing else depends. The proof network
follows the structure of the completeness proof: completeness for simple rational terms
(Lemma 6.1), the reduction of arbitrary terms to drops via lifts and the exchange lemma, and
Theorem 7.7, a provable strengthening of Theorem 2.9. The results of the appendix on which
the proofs depend are proved as auxiliary lemmas.

concepts.title: The bundle lemma
concepts.description:
**Lemma 6.7 (Bundles).** For every type $A$, there are arbitrarily large numbers $k$ such
that the concatenation map
$$
(A^k)^* \times A^{<k} \rightarrowtail A^*
$$
is an isomorphism. Here $A^i$ is the $i$-fold product of $A$ with itself, with
$A^0 = 1$, and $A^{<k}$ is the co-product of all $A^i$ with $0 \le i < k$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The bundle size is written $k + 1$, so that $A^{<k+1} = A^0 + \cdots + A^k$ is the type
constructor `TyF.lt k`. The formal statement is stronger than the paper's: the bundle
sizes $k + 1$ can be chosen independently of the type $A$.

g_1 \equiv g_2 &\quad\text{iff}\quad g_1 \mathbin{;} f \equiv g_2 \mathbin{;} f

g_1 \equiv g_2 &\quad\text{iff}\quad f \mathbin{;} g_1 \equiv f \mathbin{;} g_2
  &&\text{for every surjective } f : C \to A.
\end{aligned}
$$

concepts.title: Conjugacy completeness
concepts.description:
**Theorem 2.6 (Conjugacy completeness).** Two simple rational terms define the same function
if and only if they are equivalent with respect to the least equivalence relation $\equiv$
on simple rational terms that satisfies the following rules (where $f, g, h$ are simple
rational terms, $w, v$ are strings and $\varepsilon$ is the empty string):

1. *Congruence:* $\equiv$ is preserved by co-pairing, concatenation, homomorphism and
   adding constants.
2. *Concatenation monoidality:* $(f \cdot w) \cdot v \equiv f \cdot wv$,
   $w \cdot (v \cdot f) \equiv wv \cdot f$, $f \cdot \varepsilon \equiv f \equiv
   \varepsilon \cdot f$, $(w \cdot f) \cdot v \equiv w \cdot (f \cdot v)$,
   $(f \cdot w) \odot g \equiv f \odot (w \cdot g)$,
   $w \cdot (f \odot g) \equiv (w \cdot f) \odot g$,
   $(f \odot g) \cdot w \equiv f \odot (g \cdot w)$, and
   $[] \cdot w \equiv w \cdot []$.
3. *Constants and co-pairing:* $w \cdot \langle f_1, f_2 \rangle \equiv
   \langle w \cdot f_1, w \cdot f_2 \rangle$ and $\langle f_1, f_2 \rangle \cdot w
   \equiv \langle f_1 \cdot w, f_2 \cdot w \rangle$.
4. *Case splitting:* if $\langle f_1 \odot h, f_2 \odot h \rangle \equiv
   \langle g_1 \odot h, g_2 \odot h \rangle$ then
   $\langle f_1, f_2 \rangle \odot h \equiv \langle g_1, g_2 \rangle \odot h$, and
   symmetrically on the other side.
5. *Conjugacy:* if $f \cdot w \equiv w \cdot g$ then
   $(\mathrm{hom}\, f) \cdot w \equiv w \cdot (\mathrm{hom}\, g)$.

   $(f \cdot w) \odot g \equiv f \odot (w \cdot g)$,
   $w \cdot (f \odot g) \equiv (w \cdot f) \odot g$,
   $(f \odot g) \cdot w \equiv f \odot (g \cdot w)$, and
   $[] \cdot w \equiv w \cdot []$.
3. *Constants and co-pairing:* $w \cdot \langle f_1, f_2 \rangle \equiv

namespace Lax149335.ConjugacyCompleteness

open Lax149335.Types Lax149335.SimpleRationalTerms

namespace SimpleTerm

/-- The equivalence `≡` of simple rational terms from Theorem 2.6: the least relation closed
under (1) congruence, (2) concatenation monoidality, (3) constants and co-pairing, (4) case
splitting and (5) conjugacy. -/
inductive SEq {Bs : Type} : {A : Ty} → SimpleTerm Bs A → SimpleTerm Bs A → Prop
  -- (1) congruence, together with the equivalence relation rules
  | refl {A : Ty} (f : SimpleTerm Bs A) : SEq f f
  | symm {A : Ty} {f g : SimpleTerm Bs A} : SEq f g → SEq g f
  | trans {A : Ty} {f g h : SimpleTerm Bs A} : SEq f g → SEq g h → SEq f h
  | congr_either {A₁ A₂ : Ty} {f₁ g₁ : SimpleTerm Bs A₁} {f₂ g₂ : SimpleTerm Bs A₂} :
      SEq f₁ g₁ → SEq f₂ g₂ → SEq (.either f₁ f₂) (.either g₁ g₂)
  | congr_conc {A₁ A₂ : Ty} {f₁ g₁ : SimpleTerm Bs A₁} {f₂ g₂ : SimpleTerm Bs A₂} :
      SEq f₁ g₁ → SEq f₂ g₂ → SEq (.conc f₁ f₂) (.conc g₁ g₂)
  | congr_hom {A : Ty} {f g : SimpleTerm Bs A} : SEq f g → SEq (.hom f) (.hom g)
  | congr_pre {A : Ty} {f g : SimpleTerm Bs A} (w : List Bs) :
      SEq f g → SEq (.pre w f) (.pre w g)
  | congr_post {A : Ty} {f g : SimpleTerm Bs A} (w : List Bs) :
      SEq f g → SEq (.post f w) (.post g w)
  -- (2) concatenation monoidality
  | post_post {A : Ty} (f : SimpleTerm Bs A) (w v : List Bs) :
      SEq (.post (.post f w) v) (.post f (w ++ v))
  | pre_pre {A : Ty} (f : SimpleTerm Bs A) (w v : List Bs) :
      SEq (.pre w (.pre v f)) (.pre (w ++ v) f)
  | post_nil {A : Ty} (f : SimpleTerm Bs A) : SEq (.post f []) f
  | pre_nil {A : Ty} (f : SimpleTerm Bs A) : SEq (.pre [] f) f
  | pre_post {A : Ty} (f : SimpleTerm Bs A) (w v : List Bs) :
      SEq (.post (.pre w f) v) (.pre w (.post f v))
  | conc_shift {A₁ A₂ : Ty} (f : SimpleTerm Bs A₁) (g : SimpleTerm Bs A₂) (w : List Bs) :
      SEq (.conc (.post f w) g) (.conc f (.pre w g))
  | pre_conc {A₁ A₂ : Ty} (w : List Bs) (f₁ : SimpleTerm Bs A₁) (f₂ : SimpleTerm Bs A₂) :
      SEq (.pre w (.conc f₁ f₂)) (.conc (.pre w f₁) f₂)
  | post_conc {A₁ A₂ : Ty} (w : List Bs) (f₁ : SimpleTerm Bs A₁) (f₂ : SimpleTerm Bs A₂) :
      SEq (.post (.conc f₁ f₂) w) (.conc f₁ (.post f₂ w))
  | move_empty (w : List Bs) :
      SEq (.post (.empty : SimpleTerm Bs Ty.unit) w) (.pre w .empty)
  -- (3) constants and copairing
  | pre_either {A₁ A₂ : Ty} (w : List Bs) (f₁ : SimpleTerm Bs A₁) (f₂ : SimpleTerm Bs A₂) :
      SEq (.pre w (.either f₁ f₂)) (.either (.pre w f₁) (.pre w f₂))
  | post_either {A₁ A₂ : Ty} (w : List Bs) (f₁ : SimpleTerm Bs A₁) (f₂ : SimpleTerm Bs A₂) :
      SEq (.post (.either f₁ f₂) w) (.either (.post f₁ w) (.post f₂ w))
  -- (4) case splitting
  | case_left {A₁ A₂ A : Ty} {f₁ g₁ : SimpleTerm Bs A₁} {f₂ g₂ : SimpleTerm Bs A₂}
      {h : SimpleTerm Bs A} :
      SEq (.either (.conc f₁ h) (.conc f₂ h)) (.either (.conc g₁ h) (.conc g₂ h)) →
      SEq (.conc (.either f₁ f₂) h) (.conc (.either g₁ g₂) h)
  | case_right {A₁ A₂ A : Ty} {f₁ g₁ : SimpleTerm Bs A₁} {f₂ g₂ : SimpleTerm Bs A₂}
      {h : SimpleTerm Bs A} :
      SEq (.either (.conc h f₁) (.conc h f₂)) (.either (.conc h g₁) (.conc h g₂)) →
      SEq (.conc h (.either f₁ f₂)) (.conc h (.either g₁ g₂))
  -- (5) conjugacy
  | conjugacy {A : Ty} {f g : SimpleTerm Bs A} (w : List Bs) :
      SEq (.post f w) (.pre w g) → SEq (.post (.hom f) w) (.pre w (.hom g))

/-- Notation `f ≃ₛ g` for the equivalence of simple rational terms. -/
infix:50 " ≃ₛ " => SEq

end SimpleTerm

/-- **Theorem 2.6.** Two simple rational terms define the same function if and only if they
are equivalent. -/
axiom conjugacy_completeness {Bs : Type} {A : Ty} (f g : SimpleTerm Bs A) :
    f.den = g.den ↔ f ≃ₛ g

end Lax149335.ConjugacyCompleteness

concepts.title: The conjugacy rule for syntactic conjugates
concepts.description:
**Lemma 6.2.** For a simple rational term $h : A \to B^*$ and a value $w : 1 \to B^*$,
$$
\mathrm{hom}(w \cdot h) \cdot w \;\equiv\; w \cdot \mathrm{hom}(h \cdot w).
$$
That is, the conjugacy rule holds when its assumption is strengthened from provable to
syntactic conjugacy.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The paper states the lemma for a simple rational term over a finite alphabet. Neither
assumption is used in the proof, so the statement is formalised for an arbitrary rational
term $h : A \to B^*$, which makes it stronger.

concepts.title: Equivalence of simple rational terms is decidable
concepts.description: **Corollary 2.8.** Equivalence for simple rational terms is decidable in polynomial time.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Running time is not expressible here. The corollary is formalised by a decision procedure
that is explicit enough to make the polynomial bound evident: two simple rational terms
$f, g : A \to B^*$ define the same function if and only if they agree on a fixed finite set
$T(A)$ of *test inputs*, defined by induction on the type $A$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
T(1) &= \{()\}, &
T(A_1 + A_2) &= \mathsf{Left}\, T(A_1) \cup \mathsf{Right}\, T(A_2), \\
T(A^*) &= \{[\,]\} \cup \{[a] : a \in T(A)\}, &
T(A_1 \times A_2) &= T(A_1) \times \{e_2\} \;\cup\; \{e_1\} \times T(A_2),
\end{aligned}
$$
where $e_i$ is a fixed element of $A_i$ (`Ty.someElem`). The number of test inputs is at
most the size of $A$, every test input has size at most the size of $A$, and a simple
rational term is evaluated on an input in polynomial time.

# Formalization notes

-/

namespace Lax149335.DecidableEquivalence

open Lax149335.Types Lax149335.SimpleRationalTerms

/-- The test inputs `T(A)` of a type. -/
def testInputs : (A : Ty) → List ⟦A⟧
  | .unit => [()]
  | .sum A₁ A₂ => (testInputs A₁).map Sum.inl ++ (testInputs A₂).map Sum.inr
  | .prod A₁ A₂ =>
      (testInputs A₁).map (fun a => (a, Ty.someElem A₂)) ++
        (testInputs A₂).map (fun b => (Ty.someElem A₁, b))
  | .list A => [] :: (testInputs A).map (fun a => [a])

/-- **Corollary 2.8.** Two simple rational terms define the same function if and only if they
agree on all test inputs. -/
axiom decidable_equivalence {Bs : Type} {A : Ty} (f g : SimpleTerm Bs A) :
    f.den = g.den ↔ ∀ x ∈ testInputs A, f.den x = g.den x

end Lax149335.DecidableEquivalence

    (∀ (x : A.den), List.instMembership.mem (Lax149335.DecidableEquivalence.testInputs A) x → Eq (f.den x) (g.den x))

concepts.title: Derived terms
concepts.description:
The following terms are derived from the atomic functions and combinators of
Definition 3.1. They are used to state the axioms of Section 4 and the results of the
completeness proof.

- The unique term $A \to 1$, co-pairing $\langle f_1, f_2 \rangle = (f_1 + f_2) \mathbin{;}
  \mathsf{codiag}$, commutativity and associativity of co-products.
- The list notation of Section 4.6: the empty list $[\,] : 1 \to A^*$, $\mathsf{prepend} :
  A \times A^* \to A^*$, $\mathsf{append} : A^* \times A \to A^*$, $\mathsf{pure} : A \to
  A^*$, $\mathsf{binconcat} : A^* \times A^* \to A^*$, the homomorphism combinator
  $\mathrm{hom}\, f = f^* \mathbin{;} \mathsf{concat}$, and the concatenation
  $f \odot g = (f \times g) \mathbin{;} \mathsf{binconcat}$ of two terms with list outputs.
- The inverses of distributivity, $\mathsf{undistL}$ and $\mathsf{undistR}$ (Section 4.4).
- **Definition 5.1 (Value).** A *value* is a term of type $1 \to A$. For a list value $w$,
  the terms $w \cdot f$ and $f \cdot w$ prepend or append the output of $w$ to the output
  of $f$ (Section 5.2), and $\mathsf{head}_w : A^* \to A$ returns the first element of a
  list, or the output of $w$ for the empty list.
- *Concatenation maps* (Section 5.1). For a type constructor $F$ with one parameter, built
  from the parameter, $1$, $\times$, $+$ and $(-)^*$, the concatenation map
  $F(A) \rightarrowtail A^*$ lists all the elements of $A$ occurring in the input, from left
  to right. Similarly for type constructors with two parameters, with outputs in
  $(A + B)^*$. In particular, $\mathsf{unsplit} : A^* \times (B \times A^*)^* \to
  (A + B)^*$ is a concatenation map.
- The terms $\mathsf{shift} : (A \times B)^* \to 1 + A \times (B \times A)^* \times B$ and
  $\mathsf{unshift}$ of Table 1.

import Lax149335.Terms

/-!
---
title: Derived terms
type: definition
---
The following terms are derived from the atomic functions and combinators of
Definition 3.1. They are used to state the axioms of Section 4 and the results of the
completeness proof.

- The unique term $A \to 1$, co-pairing $\langle f_1, f_2 \rangle = (f_1 + f_2) \mathbin{;}
  \mathsf{codiag}$, commutativity and associativity of co-products.
- The list notation of Section 4.6: the empty list $[\,] : 1 \to A^*$, $\mathsf{prepend} :
  A \times A^* \to A^*$, $\mathsf{append} : A^* \times A \to A^*$, $\mathsf{pure} : A \to
  A^*$, $\mathsf{binconcat} : A^* \times A^* \to A^*$, the homomorphism combinator
  $\mathrm{hom}\, f = f^* \mathbin{;} \mathsf{concat}$, and the concatenation
  $f \odot g = (f \times g) \mathbin{;} \mathsf{binconcat}$ of two terms with list outputs.
- The inverses of distributivity, $\mathsf{undistL}$ and $\mathsf{undistR}$ (Section 4.4).
- **Definition 5.1 (Value).** A *value* is a term of type $1 \to A$. For a list value $w$,
  the terms $w \cdot f$ and $f \cdot w$ prepend or append the output of $w$ to the output
  of $f$ (Section 5.2), and $\mathsf{head}_w : A^* \to A$ returns the first element of a
  list, or the output of $w$ for the empty list.
- *Concatenation maps* (Section 5.1). For a type constructor $F$ with one parameter, built
  from the parameter, $1$, $\times$, $+$ and $(-)^*$, the concatenation map
  $F(A) \rightarrowtail A^*$ lists all the elements of $A$ occurring in the input, from left
  to right. Similarly for type constructors with two parameters, with outputs in
  $(A + B)^*$. In particular, $\mathsf{unsplit} : A^* \times (B \times A^*)^* \to
  (A + B)^*$ is a concatenation map.
- The terms $\mathsf{shift} : (A \times B)^* \to 1 + A \times (B \times A)^* \times B$ and
  $\mathsf{unshift}$ of Table 1.
- The inverse $\mathsf{unpref}$ of group prefix multiplication (Section 4.4), which maps
  $[(a_1, g_1), \ldots, (a_n, g_n)]$ to $[(a_1, g_0^{-1} g_1), \ldots, (a_n, g_{n-1}^{-1} g_n)]$,
  where $g_0$ is the group identity.

# Formalization notes

The paper only asserts that a term for $\mathsf{unpref}$ exists. Here it is defined
explicitly, following the appendix, by case analysis on the letters of the finite alphabet
that carries the group (`caseL`, `caseR`, `constFin`).
-/

namespace Lax149335.DerivedTerms

open Lax149335.Types Lax149335.Terms

namespace Term

open Lax149335.Terms.Term

/-- The unique function into the unit type, `A → 1`. -/
def toUnit (A : Ty) : Term A Ty.unit := unitL A ⨟ fst Ty.unit A

/-- Co-pairing, a derived combinator: `either f₁ f₂ = (f₁ + f₂); codiag`. -/
def either {A₁ A₂ B : Ty} (f₁ : Term A₁ B) (f₂ : Term A₂ B) : Term (A₁ ⊕' A₂) B :=
  sumF f₁ f₂ ⨟ codiag B

/-- Commutativity of the co-product, a derived term. -/
def comm (A B : Ty) : Term (A ⊕' B) (B ⊕' A) := either (inr B A) (inl B A)

/-- Associativity of the co-product, from left to right. -/
def sumAssocR (A B C : Ty) : Term ((A ⊕' B) ⊕' C) (A ⊕' (B ⊕' C)) :=
  either (either (inl A (B ⊕' C)) (inl B C ⨟ inr A (B ⊕' C))) (inr B C ⨟ inr A (B ⊕' C))

/-- Associativity of the co-product, from right to left. -/
def sumAssocL (A B C : Ty) : Term (A ⊕' (B ⊕' C)) ((A ⊕' B) ⊕' C) :=
  either (inl A B ⨟ inl (A ⊕' B) C)
    (either (inr A B ⨟ inl (A ⊕' B) C) (inr (A ⊕' B) C))

/-- The empty list `[] : 1 → A*`, defined as `Left; cons`. -/
def nilT (A : Ty) : Term Ty.unit A⋆ := inl Ty.unit (A ⊗ A⋆) ⨟ cons A

/-- `prepend : A × A* → A*`, defined as `Right; cons`. -/
def prepend (A : Ty) : Term (A ⊗ A⋆) A⋆ := inr Ty.unit (A ⊗ A⋆) ⨟ cons A

/-- `append : A* × A → A*`, defined as `Right; snoc`. -/
def append (A : Ty) : Term (A⋆ ⊗ A) A⋆ := inr Ty.unit (A⋆ ⊗ A) ⨟ snoc A

/-- `pure : A → A*`, defined as `(id,1); id × []; prepend`. -/
def pureT (A : Ty) : Term A A⋆ :=
  unitR A ⨟ prodF (Term.id A) (nilT A) ⨟ prepend A

/-- `binconcat : A* × A* → A*`, defined as `(id × pure); prepend; concat`. -/
def binconcat (A : Ty) : Term (A⋆ ⊗ A⋆) A⋆ :=
  prodF (Term.id A⋆) (pureT A⋆) ⨟ prepend A⋆ ⨟ concat A

/-- The homomorphism combinator `hom f = f*; concat`. -/
def homT {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B⋆) : Term A⋆ B⋆ := listF f ⨟ concat B

/-- Concatenation of two functions with list outputs, `f ⊙ g = (f × g); binconcat`. -/
def fdot {A₁ A₂ B : Ty} (f : Term A₁ B⋆) (g : Term A₂ B⋆) : Term (A₁ ⊗ A₂) B⋆ :=
  prodF f g ⨟ binconcat B

/-- Notation `f ⊙ g` for the concatenation of two terms with list outputs. -/
infixl:65 " ⊙ " => Term.fdot

/-- The inverse of distributivity on the right,
`undistR = either (id × Left) (id × Right)`. -/
def undistR (A B C : Ty) : Term ((A ⊗ B) ⊕' (A ⊗ C)) (A ⊗ (B ⊕' C)) :=
  either (prodF (Term.id A) (inl B C)) (prodF (Term.id A) (inr B C))

/-- The inverse of distributivity on the left. -/
def undistL (A B C : Ty) : Term ((A ⊗ C) ⊕' (B ⊗ C)) ((A ⊕' B) ⊗ C) :=
  either (prodF (inl A B) (Term.id C)) (prodF (inr A B) (Term.id C))

-- Values and concatenation with values (Section 5.2)

/-- **Definition 5.1 (Value).** A value is a term of type `1 → A`. -/
abbrev Value (A : Ty) : Type := Term Ty.unit A

/-- Pairing a value on the left with an arbitrary term: `(v,f) = (1,id); (v × f)`. -/
def pairL {A B C : Ty} (v : Value C) (f : Term A B) : Term A (C ⊗ B) :=
  unitL A ⨟ prodF v f

/-- Pairing a value on the right with an arbitrary term: `(f,v) = (id,1); (f × v)`. -/
def pairR {A B C : Ty} (f : Term A B) (v : Value C) : Term A (B ⊗ C) :=
  unitR A ⨟ prodF f v

/-- Concatenation of a list value on the left with a term with list outputs, `w · f`. -/
def dotL {A B : Ty} (w : Value B⋆) (f : Term A B⋆) : Term A B⋆ :=
  pairL w f ⨟ binconcat B

/-- Concatenation of a term with list outputs with a list value on the right, `f · w`. -/
def dotR {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B⋆) (w : Value B⋆) : Term A B⋆ :=
  pairR f w ⨟ binconcat B

/-- The singleton list value `[v] = v; pure`. -/
def sing {A : Ty} (v : Value A) : Value A⋆ := v ⨟ pureT A

/-- The *head term for `w`*: the first element of a list, or the value `w` if the list is
empty. -/
def headT {A : Ty} (w : Value A) : Term A⋆ A :=
  uncons A ⨟ either w (fst A A⋆)

-- Concatenation maps (Section 5.1)

/-- Type constructors with one parameter, used to define concatenation maps. -/
inductive TyF : Type
  /-- The parameter itself. -/
  | param : TyF
  /-- The unit type. -/
  | unit : TyF
  /-- Product of two type constructors. -/
  | prod : TyF → TyF → TyF
  /-- Co-product of two type constructors. -/
  | sum : TyF → TyF → TyF
  /-- List of a type constructor. -/
  | list : TyF → TyF

/-- The type `F(A)` obtained by substituting the type `A` for the parameter of `F`. -/
def TyF.app : TyF → Ty → Ty
  | .param, A => A
  | .unit, _ => Ty.unit
  | .prod F G, A => (F.app A) ⊗ (G.app A)
  | .sum F G, A => (F.app A) ⊕' (G.app A)
  | .list F, A => (F.app A)⋆

/-- **Concatenation maps** (Section 5.1): the term `F(A) ↣ A*` that concatenates all the
elements of the input into a single list, defined by induction on `F`. -/
def TyF.concatMap : (F : TyF) → (A : Ty) → Term (F.app A) A⋆
  | .param, A => pureT A
  | .unit, A => nilT A
  | .prod F G, A => (F.concatMap A) ⊙ (G.concatMap A)
  | .sum F G, A => either (F.concatMap A) (G.concatMap A)
  | .list F, A => homT (F.concatMap A)

/-- The type constructor `A ↦ Aᵏ`, the `k`-fold product of the parameter with itself. -/
def TyF.pow : ℕ → TyF
  | 0 => .unit
  | (k + 1) => .prod .param (TyF.pow k)

/-- The type constructor `A ↦ A⁰ + A¹ + ⋯ + Aᵏ`, i.e. `A^{<k+1}` in the notation of the
paper. -/
def TyF.lt : ℕ → TyF
  | 0 => TyF.pow 0
  | (k + 1) => .sum (TyF.lt k) (TyF.pow (k + 1))

/-- Type constructors with two parameters, used for the concatenation maps with values in
`(A + B)*` that occur in Axiom 15 and in the definition of `unsplit`. -/
inductive TyF2 : Type
  /-- The first parameter. -/
  | p1 : TyF2
  /-- The second parameter. -/
  | p2 : TyF2
  /-- The unit type. -/
  | unit : TyF2
  /-- Product of two type constructors. -/
  | prod : TyF2 → TyF2 → TyF2
  /-- Co-product of two type constructors. -/
  | sum : TyF2 → TyF2 → TyF2
  /-- List of a type constructor. -/
  | list : TyF2 → TyF2

/-- The type `F(A,B)`. -/
def TyF2.app : TyF2 → Ty → Ty → Ty
  | .p1, A, _ => A
  | .p2, _, B => B
  | .unit, _, _ => Ty.unit
  | .prod F G, A, B => (F.app A B) ⊗ (G.app A B)
  | .sum F G, A, B => (F.app A B) ⊕' (G.app A B)
  | .list F, A, B => (F.app A B)⋆

/-- The concatenation map `F(A,B) ↣ (A+B)*`, which injects the elements of `A` and of `B`
into the co-product `A + B` and concatenates all of them. -/
def TyF2.concatMap : (F : TyF2) → (A B : Ty) → Term (F.app A B) (A ⊕' B)⋆
  | .p1, A, B => inl A B ⨟ pureT (A ⊕' B)
  | .p2, A, B => inr A B ⨟ pureT (A ⊕' B)
  | .unit, A, B => nilT (A ⊕' B)
  | .prod F G, A, B => (F.concatMap A B) ⊙ (G.concatMap A B)
  | .sum F G, A, B => either (F.concatMap A B) (G.concatMap A B)
  | .list F, A, B => homT (F.concatMap A B)

/-- The inverse of `split`: it injects `A` and `B` into the co-product `A + B` and then
concatenates all resulting lists. -/
def unsplit (A B : Ty) : Term (A⋆ ⊗ (B ⊗ A⋆)⋆) (A ⊕' B)⋆ :=
  TyF2.concatMap (.prod (.list .p1) (.list (.prod .p2 (.list .p1)))) A B

-- The terms `shift` and `unshift` of Table 1

/-- The lift `shift : (A × B)* ⊸ 1 + A × (B × A)* × B`, obtained by composing `uncons`,
`assocR` and `shiftL`. -/
def shift (A B : Ty) : Term ((A ⊗ B)⋆) (Ty.unit ⊕' (A ⊗ ((B ⊗ A)⋆ ⊗ B))) :=
  uncons (A ⊗ B) ⨟
    sumF (Term.id Ty.unit) (assocR A B ((A ⊗ B)⋆) ⨟ prodF (Term.id A) (shiftL B A))

/-- The drop `unshift : 1 + A × (B × A)* × B ⇒ (A × B)*`, the inverse of `shift`. -/
def unshift (A B : Ty) : Term (Ty.unit ⊕' (A ⊗ ((B ⊗ A)⋆ ⊗ B))) ((A ⊗ B)⋆) :=
  sumF (Term.id Ty.unit) (prodF (Term.id A) (shiftR B A) ⨟ assocL A B ((A ⊗ B)⋆)) ⨟ cons (A ⊗ B)

-- Terms for finite alphabets and the inverse of the group prefix operation

/-- The value `1 → 1 + ⋯ + 1` that picks out a given letter of a finite alphabet. -/
def constFin : {n : ℕ} → ⟦Ty.finAlph n⟧ → Value (Ty.finAlph n)
  | 0, _ => Term.id Ty.unit
  | (_ + 1), .inl _ => inl Ty.unit _
  | (_ + 1), .inr g => constFin g ⨟ inr Ty.unit _

/-- Case analysis on a letter of a finite alphabet that appears as the right component of a
product; it is derived using distributivity and co-pairing. -/
def caseR : {n : ℕ} → {A B : Ty} → (⟦Ty.finAlph n⟧ → Term A B) → Term (A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n) B
  | 0, A, _, t => fst A Ty.unit ⨟ t ()
  | (n + 1), A, _, t =>
      distR A Ty.unit (Ty.finAlph n) ⨟
        either (fst A Ty.unit ⨟ t (.inl ())) (caseR (fun g => t (.inr g)))

/-- Case analysis on a letter of a finite alphabet that appears as the left component of a
product. -/
def caseL : {n : ℕ} → {A B : Ty} → (⟦Ty.finAlph n⟧ → Term A B) → Term (Ty.finAlph n ⊗ A) B
  | 0, A, _, t => snd Ty.unit A ⨟ t ()
  | (n + 1), A, _, t =>
      distL Ty.unit (Ty.finAlph n) A ⨟
        either (snd Ty.unit A ⨟ t (.inl ())) (caseL (fun g => t (.inr g)))

/-- The term `(a,g) ↦ (g,(a,g))`, admissible because the group is a finite alphabet. -/
def grepeat (A : Ty) (n : ℕ) : Term (A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n) (Ty.finAlph n ⊗ (A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n)) :=
  caseR (fun g => pairL (constFin g) (pairR (Term.id A) (constFin g)))

/-- The term `(h,(g,a)) ↦ (a, h⁻¹ · g)`, admissible because the group is a finite
alphabet. -/
def gdiv (A : Ty) {n : ℕ} (G : Group ⟦Ty.finAlph n⟧) :
    Term (Ty.finAlph n ⊗ (Ty.finAlph n ⊗ A)) (A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n) :=
  caseL (fun h => caseL (fun g => pairR (Term.id A) (constFin (letI := G; h⁻¹ * g))))

/-- The unprefixing operation, the inverse of the group prefix multiplication:
`[(a₁,g₁),…,(aₙ,gₙ)] ↦ [(a₁,g₀⁻¹g₁),(a₂,g₁⁻¹g₂),…,(aₙ,gₙ₋₁⁻¹gₙ)]`, where `g₀` is the group
identity. -/
def unpref (A : Ty) {n : ℕ} (G : Group ⟦Ty.finAlph n⟧) :
    Term ((A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n)⋆) ((A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n)⋆) :=
  listF (grepeat A n) ⨟
    listF (assocL (Ty.finAlph n) A (Ty.finAlph n)) ⨟
      pairL (constFin (letI := G; (1 : ⟦Ty.finAlph n⟧))) (Term.id _) ⨟
        shiftL (Ty.finAlph n) (Ty.finAlph n ⊗ A) ⨟
          fst _ _ ⨟ listF (gdiv A G)

end Term

end Lax149335.DerivedTerms

/-- **Lemma 7.3.** Two drops `A → N*` into the lists over a finite alphabet become provably
equivalent to simple rational terms after precomposing with the inverse of a common lift. -/
axiom drops_to_simple {A B : Ty} (hB : Ty.IsFinAlph B) (f g : Term A B⋆)
    (hf : IsDrop f) (hg : IsDrop g) :
    ∃ (C : Ty) (l : Term A C) (π : Term C A),
      IsLift l ∧ IsDrop π ∧ (l ⨟ π) ≡ₜ Term.id A ∧ (π ⨟ l) ≡ₜ Term.id C ∧
      (∃ f' : Term C B⋆, IsSimple B f' ∧ (π ⨟ f) ≡ₜ f') ∧
      (∃ g' : Term C B⋆, IsSimple B g' ∧ (π ⨟ g) ≡ₜ g')

end Lax149335.DropsJointSimplification

concepts.title: The equational theory
concepts.description:
Section 4 introduces an equivalence relation $f \equiv g$ on rational terms of the same type,
called *provable equivalence*. It is the least equivalence relation on rational terms that
contains the following sixteen axioms and is preserved by the four combinators of
Definition 3.1 (composition and functoriality of products, co-products and lists).

1. *Category axioms:* composition is associative and the identity is neutral.
2. *Functoriality:* the combinators $\times$, $+$ and $(-)^*$ preserve identities and
   composition.
3. *Naturality:* every atomic function except prefix multiplication is a natural
   transformation.
4. *Isomorphisms:* ten pairs of mutually inverse terms — the units and $\mathsf{fst}$,
   $\mathsf{snd}$; $\mathsf{assocL}$ and $\mathsf{assocR}$; $\mathsf{distL}$ and
   $\mathsf{undistL}$; $\mathsf{distR}$ and $\mathsf{undistR}$; $\mathsf{cons}$ and
   $\mathsf{uncons}$; $\mathsf{snoc}$ and $\mathsf{unsnoc}$; $\mathsf{split}$ and
   $\mathsf{unsplit}$; $\mathsf{pref}$ and $\mathsf{unpref}$; $\mathsf{shiftL}$ and
   $\mathsf{shiftR}$.
5. The unit type is terminal: any two terms $A \to 1$ are equivalent.
6. *The co-diagonal:* $\mathsf{Left} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{codiag} \equiv \mathrm{id}$,
   $\mathsf{Right} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{codiag} \equiv \mathrm{id}$ and
   $(\mathsf{Left} + \mathsf{Right}) \mathbin{;} \mathsf{codiag} \equiv \mathrm{id}$.
7. Mac Lane's pentagon for $\mathsf{assocL}$.
8. Mac Lane's triangle for $\mathsf{assocL}$ and the unit.
9. The notation based on $\mathsf{snoc}$ agrees with the notation based on
   $\mathsf{cons}$: for the empty list, for singleton lists, and for concatenation.
10. $A^*$ is a monoid under $\mathsf{binconcat}$ with unit $[\,]$.
11. $\mathsf{concat}$ is a monoid homomorphism.
12. $A^*$ is a monad with unit $\mathsf{pure}$ and multiplication $\mathsf{concat}$.
13. $\mathsf{prepend}$ and $\mathsf{append}$ are expressed by $\mathsf{binconcat}$.
14. Concatenating a list of empty lists gives the empty list.
15. $\mathsf{shiftR}$ does not change the content of a list: it commutes with the
    concatenation maps into $(A + B)^*$.
16. *The window axiom:* the bundle term
    $\mathsf{bundle} : (2^*)^* \to (2^* \times 2^*)^* \times (1 + 2^*)$, which splits a
    list into consecutive pairs followed by a remainder of at most one element, is undone by
    the concatenation map: $\mathsf{bundle} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{concat} \equiv
    \mathrm{id}$. Here $2 = 1 + 1$.

The bundle term (Definition H.5) is, for a type $A$ and a value $w : 1 \to A$, the
composition
$$
((\mathrm{id}, 1) \mathbin{;} (\mathrm{id} \times \mathsf{Right}))^* \mathbin{;}
\mathsf{pref}_{\mathbb{Z}_2} \mathbin{;}
(\mathsf{distR} \mathbin{;} \langle \mathsf{fst} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{Right},
\mathsf{fst} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{Left} \rangle)^* \mathbin{;} \mathsf{split}
\mathbin{;} \mathsf{shiftL} \mathbin{;} ((\mathsf{head}_w \times \mathrm{id})^*
\times (\mathsf{uncons} \mathbin{;} (\mathrm{id} + \mathsf{fst}))),
$$
where $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is the cyclic group of order two on $2 = 1 + 1$, with identity
$\mathsf{Left}$. The window axiom uses it for $A = 2^*$ and $w = [\,]$.

import Lax149335.DerivedTerms

/-!
---
title: The equational theory
type: definition
---
Section 4 introduces an equivalence relation $f \equiv g$ on rational terms of the same type,
called *provable equivalence*. It is the least equivalence relation on rational terms that
contains the following sixteen axioms and is preserved by the four combinators of
Definition 3.1 (composition and functoriality of products, co-products and lists).

1. *Category axioms:* composition is associative and the identity is neutral.
2. *Functoriality:* the combinators $\times$, $+$ and $(-)^*$ preserve identities and
   composition.
3. *Naturality:* every atomic function except prefix multiplication is a natural
   transformation.
4. *Isomorphisms:* ten pairs of mutually inverse terms — the units and $\mathsf{fst}$,
   $\mathsf{snd}$; $\mathsf{assocL}$ and $\mathsf{assocR}$; $\mathsf{distL}$ and
   $\mathsf{undistL}$; $\mathsf{distR}$ and $\mathsf{undistR}$; $\mathsf{cons}$ and
   $\mathsf{uncons}$; $\mathsf{snoc}$ and $\mathsf{unsnoc}$; $\mathsf{split}$ and
   $\mathsf{unsplit}$; $\mathsf{pref}$ and $\mathsf{unpref}$; $\mathsf{shiftL}$ and
   $\mathsf{shiftR}$.
5. The unit type is terminal: any two terms $A \to 1$ are equivalent.
6. *The co-diagonal:* $\mathsf{Left} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{codiag} \equiv \mathrm{id}$,
   $\mathsf{Right} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{codiag} \equiv \mathrm{id}$ and
   $(\mathsf{Left} + \mathsf{Right}) \mathbin{;} \mathsf{codiag} \equiv \mathrm{id}$.
7. Mac Lane's pentagon for $\mathsf{assocL}$.
8. Mac Lane's triangle for $\mathsf{assocL}$ and the unit.
9. The notation based on $\mathsf{snoc}$ agrees with the notation based on
   $\mathsf{cons}$: for the empty list, for singleton lists, and for concatenation.
10. $A^*$ is a monoid under $\mathsf{binconcat}$ with unit $[\,]$.
11. $\mathsf{concat}$ is a monoid homomorphism.
12. $A^*$ is a monad with unit $\mathsf{pure}$ and multiplication $\mathsf{concat}$.
13. $\mathsf{prepend}$ and $\mathsf{append}$ are expressed by $\mathsf{binconcat}$.
14. Concatenating a list of empty lists gives the empty list.
15. $\mathsf{shiftR}$ does not change the content of a list: it commutes with the
    concatenation maps into $(A + B)^*$.
16. *The window axiom:* the bundle term
    $\mathsf{bundle} : (2^*)^* \to (2^* \times 2^*)^* \times (1 + 2^*)$, which splits a
    list into consecutive pairs followed by a remainder of at most one element, is undone by
    the concatenation map: $\mathsf{bundle} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{concat} \equiv
    \mathrm{id}$. Here $2 = 1 + 1$.

The bundle term (Definition H.5) is, for a type $A$ and a value $w : 1 \to A$, the
composition
$$
((\mathrm{id}, 1) \mathbin{;} (\mathrm{id} \times \mathsf{Right}))^* \mathbin{;}
\mathsf{pref}_{\mathbb{Z}_2} \mathbin{;}
(\mathsf{distR} \mathbin{;} \langle \mathsf{fst} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{Right},
\mathsf{fst} \mathbin{;} \mathsf{Left} \rangle)^* \mathbin{;} \mathsf{split}
\mathbin{;} \mathsf{shiftL} \mathbin{;} ((\mathsf{head}_w \times \mathrm{id})^*
\times (\mathsf{uncons} \mathbin{;} (\mathrm{id} + \mathsf{fst}))),
$$
where $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is the cyclic group of order two on $2 = 1 + 1$, with identity
$\mathsf{Left}$. The window axiom uses it for $A = 2^*$ and $w = [\,]$.

# Formalization notes

Naturality of prefix multiplication is not an axiom: as observed in footnote 5 of the paper,
it is derivable. The axioms are listed in full in the constructors of `PEq` below.
-/

namespace Lax149335.EquationalTheory

open Lax149335.Types Lax149335.Terms Lax149335.DerivedTerms

namespace Term

open Lax149335.Terms.Term Lax149335.DerivedTerms.Term

/-- The cyclic group `ℤ₂` of order two, with the two letter alphabet `2 = 1 + 1` as its
underlying set: the group identity is the first letter `Left`, and the second letter `Right`
is the generator. -/
def cyclicTwo : Group ⟦Ty.finAlph 1⟧ where
  mul x y := match x, y with
    | .inl _, y => y
    | x, .inl _ => x
    | .inr _, .inr _ => .inl ()
  one := .inl ()
  inv x := x
  mul_assoc := by intro x y z; cases x <;> cases y <;> cases z <;> rfl
  one_mul := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
  mul_one := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
  inv_mul_cancel := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl

/-- The generator `Right` of the cyclic group of order two. -/
def cyclicTwoGen : ⟦Ty.finAlph 1⟧ := Sum.inr ()

/-- **Step 3 of the bundle term**, for a single element: `distR ; either (fst ; Right)
(fst ; Left) : A × 2 → A + A`.  An element annotated with the generator `Right` goes to the
left copy of `A`, and an element annotated with the identity `Left` goes to the right
copy. -/
def bundleTag (A : Ty) : Term (A ⊗ Ty.finAlph 1) (A ⊕' A) :=
  distR A Ty.unit (Ty.finAlph 0) ⨟ either (fst A Ty.unit ⨟ inr A A) (fst A Ty.unit ⨟ inl A A)

/-- **Definition H.5 (the bundle term)** `A* → (A × A)* × (1 + A)`, for a type `A` and a value
`w : 1 → A`:

`((id,1) ; (id × Right))* ; pref_{ℤ₂} ; (distR ; either (fst ; Right) (fst ; Left))* ;
split ; shiftL ; ((head_w × id)* × (uncons ; (id + fst)))`.

The window axiom (Axiom 16) says that, for `A = 2*` and `w = []`, it is a one-sided inverse
of the concatenation map `(A × A)* × (1 + A) ↣ A*`. -/
def bundle (A : Ty) (w : Value A) : Term A⋆ ((A ⊗ A)⋆ ⊗ (Ty.unit ⊕' A)) :=
  listF (unitR A ⨟ prodF (Term.id A) (inr Ty.unit (Ty.finAlph 0))) ⨟
    pref A cyclicTwo ⨟
    listF (bundleTag A) ⨟
    split A A ⨟
    shiftL A⋆ A ⨟
    prodF (listF (prodF (headT w) (Term.id A))) (uncons A ⨟ sumF (Term.id Ty.unit) (fst A A⋆))

/-- The type constructor `A ↦ (A × A)* × (1 + A)` of the window axiom. -/
def TyF.window : TyF := .prod (.list (.prod .param .param)) (.sum .unit .param)

end Term

open Lax149335.Terms.Term Lax149335.DerivedTerms.Term

/-- Provable equality of rational terms: the least equivalence relation containing
Axioms 1-16 of Section 4 and stable under the combinators of the system. -/
inductive PEq : {A B : Ty} → Term A B → Term A B → Prop
  -- rules of equational reasoning: `≡` is an equivalence relation, stable under the
  -- four combinators of the system
  | refl {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) : PEq f f
  | symm {A B : Ty} {f g : Term A B} : PEq f g → PEq g f
  | trans {A B : Ty} {f g h : Term A B} : PEq f g → PEq g h → PEq f h
  | congr_comp {A B C : Ty} {f f' : Term A B} {g g' : Term B C} :
      PEq f f' → PEq g g' → PEq (f ⨟ g) (f' ⨟ g')
  | congr_prodF {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ : Ty} {f f' : Term A₁ B₁} {g g' : Term A₂ B₂} :
      PEq f f' → PEq g g' → PEq (prodF f g) (prodF f' g')
  | congr_sumF {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ : Ty} {f f' : Term A₁ B₁} {g g' : Term A₂ B₂} :
      PEq f f' → PEq g g' → PEq (sumF f g) (sumF f' g')
  | congr_listF {A B : Ty} {f f' : Term A B} : PEq f f' → PEq (listF f) (listF f')
  -- ## Axiom 1 (category axioms)
  | comp_assoc {A B C D : Ty} (f : Term A B) (g : Term B C) (h : Term C D) :
      PEq ((f ⨟ g) ⨟ h) (f ⨟ (g ⨟ h))
  | id_comp {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) : PEq (Term.id A ⨟ f) f
  | comp_id {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) : PEq (f ⨟ Term.id B) f
  -- ## Axiom 2 (functoriality), first part: the functors preserve the identity
  | prod_id (A B : Ty) : PEq (prodF (Term.id A) (Term.id B)) (Term.id (A ⊗ B))
  | sum_id (A B : Ty) : PEq (sumF (Term.id A) (Term.id B)) (Term.id (A ⊕' B))
  | list_id (A : Ty) : PEq (listF (Term.id A)) (Term.id A⋆)
  -- ## Axiom 2 (functoriality), second part: the functors preserve composition
  | prod_comp {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ C₁ C₂ : Ty} (f₁ : Term A₁ B₁) (f₂ : Term A₂ B₂)
      (g₁ : Term B₁ C₁) (g₂ : Term B₂ C₂) :
      PEq (prodF f₁ f₂ ⨟ prodF g₁ g₂) (prodF (f₁ ⨟ g₁) (f₂ ⨟ g₂))
  | sum_comp {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ C₁ C₂ : Ty} (f₁ : Term A₁ B₁) (f₂ : Term A₂ B₂)
      (g₁ : Term B₁ C₁) (g₂ : Term B₂ C₂) :
      PEq (sumF f₁ f₂ ⨟ sumF g₁ g₂) (sumF (f₁ ⨟ g₁) (f₂ ⨟ g₂))
  | list_comp {A B C : Ty} (f : Term A B) (g : Term B C) :
      PEq (listF f ⨟ listF g) (listF (f ⨟ g))
  -- ## Axiom 3 (each atomic function is a natural transformation)
  | nat_inl {A A' B B' : Ty} (f : Term A A') (g : Term B B') :
      PEq (inl A B ⨟ sumF f g) (f ⨟ inl A' B')
  | nat_inr {A A' B B' : Ty} (f : Term A A') (g : Term B B') :
      PEq (inr A B ⨟ sumF f g) (g ⨟ inr A' B')
  | nat_codiag {A A' : Ty} (f : Term A A') :
      PEq (sumF f f ⨟ codiag A') (codiag A ⨟ f)
  | nat_fst {A A' B B' : Ty} (f : Term A A') (g : Term B B') :
      PEq (prodF f g ⨟ fst A' B') (fst A B ⨟ f)
  | nat_snd {A A' B B' : Ty} (f : Term A A') (g : Term B B') :
      PEq (prodF f g ⨟ snd A' B') (snd A B ⨟ g)
  | nat_unitR {A A' : Ty} (f : Term A A') :
      PEq (f ⨟ unitR A') (unitR A ⨟ prodF f (Term.id Ty.unit))
  | nat_unitL {A A' : Ty} (f : Term A A') :
      PEq (f ⨟ unitL A') (unitL A ⨟ prodF (Term.id Ty.unit) f)
  | nat_assocL {A A' B B' C C' : Ty} (f₁ : Term A A') (f₂ : Term B B') (f₃ : Term C C') :
      PEq (prodF f₁ (prodF f₂ f₃) ⨟ assocL A' B' C') (assocL A B C ⨟ prodF (prodF f₁ f₂) f₃)
  | nat_assocR {A A' B B' C C' : Ty} (f₁ : Term A A') (f₂ : Term B B') (f₃ : Term C C') :
      PEq (prodF (prodF f₁ f₂) f₃ ⨟ assocR A' B' C') (assocR A B C ⨟ prodF f₁ (prodF f₂ f₃))
  | nat_distR {A A' B B' C C' : Ty} (f : Term A A') (g : Term B B') (h : Term C C') :
      PEq (prodF f (sumF g h) ⨟ distR A' B' C') (distR A B C ⨟ sumF (prodF f g) (prodF f h))
  | nat_distL {A A' B B' C C' : Ty} (f : Term A A') (g : Term B B') (h : Term C C') :
      PEq (prodF (sumF f g) h ⨟ distL A' B' C') (distL A B C ⨟ sumF (prodF f h) (prodF g h))
  | nat_cons {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) :
      PEq (sumF (Term.id Ty.unit) (prodF f (listF f)) ⨟ cons B) (cons A ⨟ listF f)
  | nat_uncons {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) :
      PEq (listF f ⨟ uncons B) (uncons A ⨟ sumF (Term.id Ty.unit) (prodF f (listF f)))
  | nat_snoc {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) :
      PEq (sumF (Term.id Ty.unit) (prodF (listF f) f) ⨟ snoc B) (snoc A ⨟ listF f)
  | nat_unsnoc {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) :
      PEq (listF f ⨟ unsnoc B) (unsnoc A ⨟ sumF (Term.id Ty.unit) (prodF (listF f) f))
  | nat_concat {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) :
      PEq (listF (listF f) ⨟ concat B) (concat A ⨟ listF f)
  | nat_split {A A' B B' : Ty} (f : Term A A') (g : Term B B') :
      PEq (listF (sumF f g) ⨟ split A' B')
        (split A B ⨟ prodF (listF f) (listF (prodF g (listF f))))
  | nat_shiftR {A A' B B' : Ty} (f : Term A A') (g : Term B B') :
      PEq (prodF (listF (prodF f g)) f ⨟ shiftR A' B')
        (shiftR A B ⨟ prodF f (listF (prodF g f)))
  | nat_shiftL {A A' B B' : Ty} (f : Term A A') (g : Term B B') :
      PEq (prodF f (listF (prodF g f)) ⨟ shiftL A' B')
        (shiftL A B ⨟ prodF (listF (prodF f g)) f)
  -- (Naturality of the group prefix multiplication need not be postulated: it is derivable,
  -- see footnote 5 of the paper.)
  -- ## Axiom 4 (ten pairs of mutually inverse functions)
  | unitR_fst (A : Ty) : PEq (unitR A ⨟ fst A Ty.unit) (Term.id A)
  | fst_unitR (A : Ty) : PEq (fst A Ty.unit ⨟ unitR A) (Term.id (A ⊗ Ty.unit))
  | unitL_snd (A : Ty) : PEq (unitL A ⨟ snd Ty.unit A) (Term.id A)
  | snd_unitL (A : Ty) : PEq (snd Ty.unit A ⨟ unitL A) (Term.id (Ty.unit ⊗ A))
  | assocL_assocR (A B C : Ty) :
      PEq (assocL A B C ⨟ assocR A B C) (Term.id (A ⊗ (B ⊗ C)))
  | assocR_assocL (A B C : Ty) :
      PEq (assocR A B C ⨟ assocL A B C) (Term.id ((A ⊗ B) ⊗ C))
  | distL_undistL (A B C : Ty) :
      PEq (distL A B C ⨟ undistL A B C) (Term.id ((A ⊕' B) ⊗ C))
  | undistL_distL (A B C : Ty) :
      PEq (undistL A B C ⨟ distL A B C) (Term.id ((A ⊗ C) ⊕' (B ⊗ C)))
  | distR_undistR (A B C : Ty) :
      PEq (distR A B C ⨟ undistR A B C) (Term.id (A ⊗ (B ⊕' C)))
  | undistR_distR (A B C : Ty) :
      PEq (undistR A B C ⨟ distR A B C) (Term.id ((A ⊗ B) ⊕' (A ⊗ C)))
  | cons_uncons (A : Ty) : PEq (cons A ⨟ uncons A) (Term.id (Ty.unit ⊕' (A ⊗ A⋆)))
  | uncons_cons (A : Ty) : PEq (uncons A ⨟ cons A) (Term.id A⋆)
  | snoc_unsnoc (A : Ty) : PEq (snoc A ⨟ unsnoc A) (Term.id (Ty.unit ⊕' (A⋆ ⊗ A)))
  | unsnoc_snoc (A : Ty) : PEq (unsnoc A ⨟ snoc A) (Term.id A⋆)
  | split_unsplit (A B : Ty) : PEq (split A B ⨟ unsplit A B) (Term.id (A ⊕' B)⋆)
  | unsplit_split (A B : Ty) : PEq (unsplit A B ⨟ split A B) (Term.id (A⋆ ⊗ (B ⊗ A⋆)⋆))
  | pref_unpref (A : Ty) {n : ℕ} (G : Group ⟦Ty.finAlph n⟧) :
      PEq (pref A G ⨟ unpref A G) (Term.id ((A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n)⋆))
  | unpref_pref (A : Ty) {n : ℕ} (G : Group ⟦Ty.finAlph n⟧) :
      PEq (unpref A G ⨟ pref A G) (Term.id ((A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n)⋆))
  | shiftL_shiftR (A B : Ty) : PEq (shiftL A B ⨟ shiftR A B) (Term.id (A ⊗ (B ⊗ A)⋆))
  | shiftR_shiftL (A B : Ty) : PEq (shiftR A B ⨟ shiftL A B) (Term.id ((A ⊗ B)⋆ ⊗ A))
  -- ## Axiom 5 (the unit type is terminal)
  | unit_unique {A : Ty} (f g : Term A Ty.unit) : PEq f g
  -- ## Axiom 6 (the co-diagonal)
  | inl_codiag (A : Ty) : PEq (inl A A ⨟ codiag A) (Term.id A)
  | inr_codiag (A : Ty) : PEq (inr A A ⨟ codiag A) (Term.id A)
  | sum_inl_inr_codiag (A B : Ty) :
      PEq (sumF (inl A B) (inr A B) ⨟ codiag (A ⊕' B)) (Term.id (A ⊕' B))
  -- ## Axiom 7 (Mac Lane's pentagon)
  | pentagon (A B C D : Ty) :
      PEq (prodF (Term.id A) (assocL B C D) ⨟ assocL A (B ⊗ C) D ⨟
              prodF (assocL A B C) (Term.id D))
        (assocL A B (C ⊗ D) ⨟ assocL (A ⊗ B) C D)
  -- ## Axiom 8 (Mac Lane's triangle)
  | triangle (A C : Ty) :
      PEq (assocL A Ty.unit C ⨟ prodF (fst A Ty.unit) (Term.id C))
        (prodF (Term.id A) (snd Ty.unit C))
  -- ## Axiom 9 (`snoc`-based notation agrees with `cons`-based notation)
  | inl_snoc_cons (A : Ty) :
      PEq (inl Ty.unit (A⋆ ⊗ A) ⨟ snoc A) (inl Ty.unit (A ⊗ A⋆) ⨟ cons A)
  | append_nil_prepend_nil (A : Ty) :
      PEq (unitL A ⨟ prodF (nilT A) (Term.id A) ⨟ append A)
        (unitR A ⨟ prodF (Term.id A) (nilT A) ⨟ prepend A)
  | append_concat_prepend_concat (A : Ty) :
      PEq (prodF (pureT A⋆) (Term.id A⋆) ⨟ append A⋆ ⨟ concat A)
        (prodF (Term.id A⋆) (pureT A⋆) ⨟ prepend A⋆ ⨟ concat A)
  -- ## Axiom 10 (`A*` is a monoid)
  | binconcat_assoc (A : Ty) :
      PEq (prodF (binconcat A) (Term.id A⋆) ⨟ binconcat A)
        (assocR A⋆ A⋆ A⋆ ⨟ prodF (Term.id A⋆) (binconcat A) ⨟ binconcat A)
  | binconcat_unitR (A : Ty) :
      PEq (unitR A⋆ ⨟ prodF (Term.id A⋆) (nilT A) ⨟ binconcat A) (Term.id A⋆)
  | binconcat_unitL (A : Ty) :
      PEq (unitL A⋆ ⨟ prodF (nilT A) (Term.id A⋆) ⨟ binconcat A) (Term.id A⋆)
  -- ## Axiom 11 (`concat` is a monoid homomorphism)
  | nil_concat (A : Ty) : PEq (nilT A⋆ ⨟ concat A) (nilT A)
  | binconcat_concat (A : Ty) :
      PEq (binconcat A⋆ ⨟ concat A) (prodF (concat A) (concat A) ⨟ binconcat A)
  -- ## Axiom 12 (`A*` is a monad)
  | concat_concat (A : Ty) : PEq (listF (concat A) ⨟ concat A) (concat A⋆ ⨟ concat A)
  | pure_concat (A : Ty) : PEq (pureT A⋆ ⨟ concat A) (Term.id A⋆)
  | listF_pure_concat (A : Ty) : PEq (listF (pureT A) ⨟ concat A) (Term.id A⋆)
  -- ## Axiom 13 (the inductive structure in terms of the monoid structure)
  | prepend_def (A : Ty) :
      PEq (prepend A) (prodF (pureT A) (Term.id A⋆) ⨟ binconcat A)
  | append_def (A : Ty) :
      PEq (append A) (prodF (Term.id A⋆) (pureT A) ⨟ binconcat A)
  -- ## Axiom 14 (concatenating a list of empty lists)
  | nil_map_concat (A : Ty) :
      PEq (listF (nilT A) ⨟ concat A) (toUnit Ty.unit⋆ ⨟ nilT A)
  -- ## Axiom 15 (`shiftR` does not change the content of the list)
  | shiftR_content (A B : Ty) :
      PEq (shiftR A B ⨟ TyF2.concatMap (.prod .p1 (.list (.prod .p2 .p1))) A B)
        (TyF2.concatMap (.prod (.list (.prod .p1 .p2)) .p1) A B)
  -- ## Axiom 16 (the window axiom: the bundle term undoes the concatenation map of bundles
  -- of size two over binary strings)
  --
  -- The bundle term `bundle_{2*} : (2*)* → (2* × 2*)* × (1 + 2*)` of Definition H.5,
  -- formalised as `Term.bundle` with the value `w = []`, splits a list into bundles
  -- of two consecutive entries followed by a remainder of at most one entry.  The axiom says
  -- that this splitting is undone by the concatenation map
  --
  --   `(2* × 2*)* × (1 + 2*) ↣ (2*)*`,
  --
  -- i.e. that `bundle ; concat ≡ id`.
  | window :
      PEq (Term.bundle ((Ty.finAlph 1)⋆) (nilT (Ty.finAlph 1)) ⨟
            TyF.concatMap Term.TyF.window ((Ty.finAlph 1)⋆))
        (Term.id (((Ty.finAlph 1)⋆)⋆))

/-- Notation `f ≡ₜ g` for provable equivalence of rational terms. -/
infix:50 " ≡ₜ " => PEq

end Lax149335.EquationalTheory

import Lax149335.LiftsAndDrops
import Lax149335.EquationalTheory

/-!
---
title: Exchange
type: lemma
---
**Lemma 7.5 (Exchange).** Every composition of the form drop-lift is equivalent to a
composition of the form lift-drop.

concepts.title: Reduction to co-pairings of guarded terms
concepts.description:
**Lemma 6.4.** In the proof of the conjugacy rule of Lemma 6.1, let $k \geq 1$ be the length
of $w$. Without loss of generality, $f$ and $g$ are co-pairings
$$
\langle f_1, \ldots, f_n \rangle \quad\text{and}\quad \langle g_1, \ldots, g_n \rangle
\qquad\text{for some $k$-guarded terms } f_i, g_i : A_i \to B^*.
$$

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The "without loss of generality" is formalised as a reduction: if the conjugacy rule
$f \cdot w \equiv w \cdot g \Rightarrow (\mathrm{hom}\, f) \cdot w \equiv w \cdot
(\mathrm{hom}\, g)$ holds for all such co-pairings, then it holds for all simple rational
terms $f, g : A \to B^*$. The proof of Lemma 6.1 is an induction on the nesting depth of
lists in the input type, so the reduction is stated with the additional guarantee that the
co-pairings have an input type whose nesting depth is at most that of $A$. The assumption
that $B$ is a finite alphabet is not needed.

      dotR (copair f₀ fs) w ≡ₜ dotL w (copair g₀ gs) →

concepts.title: Guarded terms
concepts.description:
**Definition 6.3.** Let $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots\}$. A term $f : A \to B^*$ is *$k$-guarded*
if it is either

1. *constant*: the composition of the unique term $A \to 1$ with a value; or
2. *long*: of the form $u \cdot h \cdot v$ for values $u, v$ of length $k$ and a simple
   rational term $h$.

A term $f : A \to B^*$ is *nonempty* if it never produces the empty list.

The reductions of Lemmas 6.4 and 6.5 are about $n$-ary co-pairings
$\langle f_1, \ldots, f_n \rangle : A_1 + \cdots + A_n \to B^*$ of such terms, and about the
*nesting depth* of the list constructor in a type, on which the proof of Lemma 6.1 is an
induction.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
An $n$-ary co-pairing, for $n \geq 1$, is given by its first term
$f_1 : A_1 \to B^*$ and the list of the remaining terms (`Cases`); its input type
$A_1 + (A_2 + \cdots + A_n)$ is `sumTyOf A₁ [A₂, …, Aₙ]`.

# Formalization notes

An $n$-ary co-pairing, for $n \geq 1$, is given by its first term
$f_1 : A_1 \to B^*$ and the list of the remaining terms (`Cases`); its input type
$A_1 + (A_2 + \cdots + A_n)$ is `sumTyOf A₁ [A₂, …, Aₙ]`.
-/

namespace Lax149335.GuardedTerms

open Lax149335.Types Lax149335.Terms Lax149335.DerivedTerms Lax149335.DerivedTerms.Term
  Lax149335.SimpleRationalWithinSyntax

/-- **Definition 6.3.** `f : A → B*` is `k`-guarded if it is constant, or of the form
`u · h · v` for values `u`, `v` of length `k` and a simple rational term `h`. -/
def KGuarded (k : ℕ) (B : Ty) {A : Ty} (f : Term A B⋆) : Prop :=
  (∃ v : Value B⋆, f = toUnit A ⨟ v) ∨
  (∃ (u v : Value B⋆) (h : Term A B⋆),
      IsSimple B h ∧ valLength u = k ∧ valLength v = k ∧ f = dotR (dotL u h) v)

/-- A term with list outputs is nonempty if it never produces the empty list. -/
def NonemptyOutput {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B⋆) : Prop := ∀ a : ⟦A⟧, f.den a ≠ []

/-- The co-product `A₀ + (A₁ + ⋯ + Aₙ)` of a nonempty list of types. -/
def sumTyOf : Ty → List Ty → Ty
  | A, [] => A
  | A, (A' :: As) => A ⊕' sumTyOf A' As

/-- A list of terms `Aᵢ → B`, one for each type in a list of types. -/
inductive Cases (B : Ty) : List Ty → Type
  /-- The empty list of terms. -/
  | nil : Cases B []
  /-- One more term. -/
  | cons {A : Ty} {As : List Ty} : Term A B → Cases B As → Cases B (A :: As)

/-- The `n`-ary co-pairing `⟨f₀, f₁, …, fₙ⟩ : A₀ + (A₁ + ⋯ + Aₙ) → B`. -/
def copair {B : Ty} : {A : Ty} → {As : List Ty} → Term A B → Cases B As →
    Term (sumTyOf A As) B
  | _, [], f, _ => f
  | _, _ :: _, f, .cons g rest => Term.either f (copair g rest)

/-- A property holds for all terms in a list of terms. -/
def Cases.All {B : Ty} (P : (A : Ty) → Term A B → Prop) :
    {As : List Ty} → Cases B As → Prop
  | [], _ => True
  | _ :: _, .cons f rest => P _ f ∧ Cases.All P rest

/-- The nesting depth of the list constructor in a type. -/
def Ty.listDepth : Ty → ℕ
  | .unit => 0
  | .prod A B => max (Ty.listDepth A) (Ty.listDepth B)
  | .sum A B => max (Ty.listDepth A) (Ty.listDepth B)
  | .list A => Ty.listDepth A + 1

end Lax149335.GuardedTerms

concepts.title: Injective, surjective and isomorphic terms
concepts.description:
**Definition 5.4.** A rational term $f : A \to B$ is

- *injective* if $f \mathbin{;} f^{-1} \equiv \mathrm{id}$ for some term $f^{-1} : B \to A$;
- *surjective* if $f^{-1} \mathbin{;} f \equiv \mathrm{id}$ for some term
  $f^{-1} : B \to A$;
- an *isomorphism* if both hold for the same term $f^{-1}$.

In categorical terms, an injective term is a section and a surjective term is a retraction
in the category of rational terms modulo $\equiv$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The notions are called `ProvablyInjective`, `ProvablySurjective` and `ProvableIso`, to
distinguish them from injectivity and surjectivity of the denotation.

import Lax149335.EquationalTheory

/-!
---
title: Injective, surjective and isomorphic terms
type: definition
---
**Definition 5.4.** A rational term $f : A \to B$ is

- *injective* if $f \mathbin{;} f^{-1} \equiv \mathrm{id}$ for some term $f^{-1} : B \to A$;
- *surjective* if $f^{-1} \mathbin{;} f \equiv \mathrm{id}$ for some term
  $f^{-1} : B \to A$;
- an *isomorphism* if both hold for the same term $f^{-1}$.

In categorical terms, an injective term is a section and a surjective term is a retraction
in the category of rational terms modulo $\equiv$.

# Formalization notes

The notions are called `ProvablyInjective`, `ProvablySurjective` and `ProvableIso`, to
distinguish them from injectivity and surjectivity of the denotation.
-/

namespace Lax149335.InjectiveSurjectiveTerms

open Lax149335.Types Lax149335.Terms Lax149335.EquationalTheory

/-- `f : A → B` is injective if `f ; f' ≡ id` for some `f' : B → A`. -/
def ProvablyInjective {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) : Prop :=
  ∃ f' : Term B A, (f ⨟ f') ≡ₜ Term.id A

/-- `f : A → B` is surjective if `f' ; f ≡ id` for some `f' : B → A`. -/
def ProvablySurjective {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) : Prop :=
  ∃ f' : Term B A, (f' ⨟ f) ≡ₜ Term.id B

/-- `f : A → B` is an isomorphism if `f ; f' ≡ id` and `f' ; f ≡ id` for some
`f' : B → A`. -/
def ProvableIso {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) : Prop :=
  ∃ f' : Term B A, (f ⨟ f') ≡ₜ Term.id A ∧ (f' ⨟ f) ≡ₜ Term.id B

end Lax149335.InjectiveSurjectiveTerms

concepts.title: Lifts and drops
concepts.description:
**Definition 7.1 (Lifts and drops).** *Lift* terms (respectively, *drop* terms) are those
which can be obtained from the atomic lift (respectively, atomic drop) terms in Table 1 by
applying composition, as well as the functoriality combinators for co-products, products and
lists.

**Table 1.** The atomic lift terms are
$$
\begin{gathered}
A \xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}} A \qquad A + B \xrightarrow{\mathsf{comm}} B + A \qquad
A \to A \times 1 \qquad A \to 1 \times A \\
A \times (B \times C) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{assocL}} (A \times B) \times C \qquad
(A \times B) \times C \xrightarrow{\mathsf{assocR}} A \times (B \times C) \\
A + (B + C) \to (A + B) + C \qquad (A + B) + C \to A + (B + C) \\
(A + B) \times C \xrightarrow{\mathsf{distL}} A \times C + B \times C \qquad
A \times (B + C) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{distR}} A \times B + A \times C \\
(A + B)^* \xrightarrow{\mathsf{split}} A^* \times (B \times A^*)^* \qquad
(A \times B)^* \xrightarrow{\mathsf{shift}} 1 + A \times (B \times A)^* \times B
\end{gathered}
$$
and the atomic drop terms are
$$
\begin{gathered}
A \xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}} A \qquad A \xrightarrow{1 \,;\, v} B \qquad
A \times B \xrightarrow{\mathsf{fst}} A \qquad A \times B \xrightarrow{\mathsf{snd}} B
\qquad A \xrightarrow{\mathsf{Left}} A + B \qquad B \xrightarrow{\mathsf{Right}} A + B \\
\mathsf{assocL} \qquad \mathsf{assocR} \qquad A + A \xrightarrow{\mathsf{codiag}} A
\qquad A \xrightarrow{\mathsf{pure}} A^* \qquad A^{**} \xrightarrow{\mathsf{concat}} A^*
\qquad A^* \times A^* \xrightarrow{\mathsf{binconcat}} A^* \\
A \times (B \times A)^* \times B \xrightarrow{\mathsf{unshift}} (A \times B)^*
\end{gathered}
$$
where $1 \,;\, v$ is the unique term $A \to 1$ followed by an arbitrary value
$v : 1 \to B$.

  | comp {A B C : Ty} {f : Term A B} {g : Term B C} : IsLift f → IsLift g → IsLift (f ⨟ g)
  /-- Lifts are closed under functoriality of products. -/
  | prodF {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ : Ty} {f : Term A₁ B₁} {g : Term A₂ B₂} :
      IsLift f → IsLift g → IsLift (Term.prodF f g)
  /-- Lifts are closed under functoriality of co-products. -/
  | sumF {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ : Ty} {f : Term A₁ B₁} {g : Term A₂ B₂} :
      IsLift f → IsLift g → IsLift (Term.sumF f g)
  /-- Lifts are closed under functoriality of lists. -/
  | listF {A B : Ty} {f : Term A B} : IsLift f → IsLift (Term.listF f)
  /-- The identity is a prime lift. -/
  | id (A : Ty) : IsLift (Term.id A)
  /-- `(id,1)` is a prime lift. -/
  | unitR (A : Ty) : IsLift (Term.unitR A)
  /-- `(1,id)` is a prime lift. -/
  | unitL (A : Ty) : IsLift (Term.unitL A)
  /-- `assocL` is a prime lift. -/
  | assocL (A B C : Ty) : IsLift (Term.assocL A B C)
  /-- `assocR` is a prime lift. -/
  | assocR (A B C : Ty) : IsLift (Term.assocR A B C)
  /-- Associativity of the co-product, from right to left, is a prime lift. -/
  | sumAssocL (A B C : Ty) : IsLift (Term.sumAssocL A B C)
  /-- Associativity of the co-product, from left to right, is a prime lift. -/
  | sumAssocR (A B C : Ty) : IsLift (Term.sumAssocR A B C)
  /-- Commutativity of the co-product is a prime lift. -/
  | comm (A B : Ty) : IsLift (Term.comm A B)
  /-- `distL` is a prime lift. -/
  | distL (A B C : Ty) : IsLift (Term.distL A B C)
  /-- `distR` is a prime lift. -/
  | distR (A B C : Ty) : IsLift (Term.distR A B C)
  /-- `split` is a prime lift. -/
  | split (A B : Ty) : IsLift (Term.split A B)
  /-- `shift` is a prime lift. -/
  | shift (A B : Ty) : IsLift (Term.shift A B)

/-- **Definition 7.1 (Drops).** The terms obtained from the atomic drop terms of Table 1 by
composition and the functoriality combinators of products, co-products and lists. -/
inductive IsDrop : {A B : Ty} → Term A B → Prop
  /-- Drops are closed under composition. -/
  | comp {A B C : Ty} {f : Term A B} {g : Term B C} : IsDrop f → IsDrop g → IsDrop (f ⨟ g)
  /-- Drops are closed under functoriality of products. -/
  | prodF {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ : Ty} {f : Term A₁ B₁} {g : Term A₂ B₂} :
      IsDrop f → IsDrop g → IsDrop (Term.prodF f g)
  /-- Drops are closed under functoriality of co-products. -/
  | sumF {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ : Ty} {f : Term A₁ B₁} {g : Term A₂ B₂} :
      IsDrop f → IsDrop g → IsDrop (Term.sumF f g)
  /-- Drops are closed under functoriality of lists. -/
  | listF {A B : Ty} {f : Term A B} : IsDrop f → IsDrop (Term.listF f)
  /-- The identity is a prime drop. -/
  | id (A : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.id A)
  /-- A constant function `1 ; v`, for an arbitrary value `v`, is a prime drop. -/
  | bangV (A : Ty) {B : Ty} (v : Value B) : IsDrop (Term.toUnit A ⨟ v)
  /-- `assocL` is a prime drop. -/
  | assocL (A B C : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.assocL A B C)
  /-- `assocR` is a prime drop. -/
  | assocR (A B C : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.assocR A B C)
  /-- `fst` is a prime drop. -/
  | fst (A B : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.fst A B)
  /-- `snd` is a prime drop. -/
  | snd (A B : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.snd A B)
  /-- `Left` is a prime drop. -/
  | inl (A B : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.inl A B)
  /-- `Right` is a prime drop. -/
  | inr (A B : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.inr A B)
  /-- The co-diagonal is a prime drop. -/
  | codiag (A : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.codiag A)
  /-- `pure` is a prime drop. -/
  | pureT (A : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.pureT A)
  /-- `binconcat` is a prime drop. -/
  | binconcat (A : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.binconcat A)
  /-- `concat` is a prime drop. -/
  | concat (A : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.concat A)
  /-- `unshift` is a prime drop. -/
  | unshift (A B : Ty) : IsDrop (Term.unshift A B)

end Lax149335.LiftsAndDrops

$f, g : A \to N^*$, where $N$ is a finite alphabet. There is a type $B$ and a surjective
rational term $\pi : B \to A$, such that $\pi \mathbin{;} f$ and $\pi \mathbin{;} g$ are

/-- **Theorem 7.7.** Two terms `A → N*` into the
lists over a finite alphabet become provably equivalent to simple rational terms after
precomposing with a common surjective term `π : B → A`. -/
axiom provable_simplification {A N : Ty} (hN : Ty.IsFinAlph N) (f g : Term A N⋆) :
    ∃ (B : Ty) (π : Term B A), ProvablySurjective π ∧
      (∃ f' : Term B N⋆, IsSimple N f' ∧ (π ⨟ f) ≡ₜ f') ∧
      (∃ g' : Term B N⋆, IsSimple N g' ∧ (π ⨟ g) ≡ₜ g')

end Lax149335.ProvableSimplification

concepts.title: Rational functions
concepts.description:
A *rational relation* $R \subseteq A^* \times B^*$ between strings over alphabets $A$ and
$B$ is a subset of the monoid $A^* \times B^*$ defined by a regular expression: the atoms
are pairs of strings, and the operations are union, concatenation (componentwise) and Kleene
star.

**Definition 2.1 (Rational function).** A function $f : A^* \to B^*$ is *rational* if its
graph is a rational relation.

**Definition 2.3 (Rational functions on types).** A function $f : A \to B$ between types is
*rational* if there is a rational function $f' : \mathbb{8}^* \to \mathbb{8}^*$ that agrees
with $f$ on the string representations of elements, i.e. the string representation of
$f(a)$ is $f'$ applied to the string representation of $a$.

import Mathlib.Data.Set.Defs

/-!
---
title: Rational functions
type: definition
---
A *rational relation* $R \subseteq A^* \times B^*$ between strings over alphabets $A$ and
$B$ is a subset of the monoid $A^* \times B^*$ defined by a regular expression: the atoms
are pairs of strings, and the operations are union, concatenation (componentwise) and Kleene
star.

**Definition 2.1 (Rational function).** A function $f : A^* \to B^*$ is *rational* if its
graph is a rational relation.

**Definition 2.3 (Rational functions on types).** A function $f : A \to B$ between types is
*rational* if there is a rational function $f' : \mathbb{8}^* \to \mathbb{8}^*$ that agrees
with $f$ on the string representations of elements, i.e. the string representation of
$f(a)$ is $f'$ applied to the string representation of $a$.
-/

namespace Lax149335.RationalFunctions

open Lax149335.Types

variable {α β : Type}

/-- Regular expressions over the product monoid `α* × β*`. -/
inductive RatExp (α β : Type) : Type
  | zero : RatExp α β
  | atom : List α → List β → RatExp α β
  | plus : RatExp α β → RatExp α β → RatExp α β
  | cat : RatExp α β → RatExp α β → RatExp α β
  | star : RatExp α β → RatExp α β

/-- The submonoid of `α* × β*` generated by a set `S`: all finite products of elements of
`S`. -/
inductive StarSet (S : Set (List α × List β)) : List α × List β → Prop
  | nil : StarSet S ([], [])
  | cons {x y : List α × List β} : x ∈ S → StarSet S y → StarSet S (x.1 ++ y.1, x.2 ++ y.2)

/-- The relation defined by a regular expression. -/
def RatExp.lang : RatExp α β → Set (List α × List β)
  | .zero => ∅
  | .atom u v => {(u, v)}
  | .plus e f => e.lang ∪ f.lang
  | .cat e f => {p | ∃ x ∈ e.lang, ∃ y ∈ f.lang, p = (x.1 ++ y.1, x.2 ++ y.2)}
  | .star e => {p | StarSet e.lang p}

/-- A relation between strings is rational if it is defined by a regular expression. -/
def IsRationalRel (R : Set (List α × List β)) : Prop := ∃ e : RatExp α β, e.lang = R

/-- **Definition 2.1.** A function `f : α* → β*` is rational if its graph is a rational
relation. -/
def IsRationalFun (f : List α → List β) : Prop :=
  IsRationalRel {p : List α × List β | p.2 = f p.1}

/-- **Definition 2.3.** A function between types is rational if, on string representations,
it is computed by a rational function `𝟖* → 𝟖*`. -/
def IsRationalTypeFun {A B : Ty} (f : ⟦A⟧ → ⟦B⟧) : Prop :=
  ∃ f' : List Ty.Sym → List Ty.Sym,
    IsRationalFun f' ∧ ∀ a : ⟦A⟧, Ty.repr B (f a) = f' (Ty.repr A a)

end Lax149335.RationalFunctions

concepts.description:
**Definition 2.5 (Simple rational terms).** Let $B$ be a finite alphabet. The *simple
rational terms* with outputs in $B^*$ are the terms generated from the term
$[] : 1 \to B^*$, which produces the empty string, by the following combinators:

- *co-pairing*: for $f_1 : A_1 \to B^*$ and $f_2 : A_2 \to B^*$, the term
  $\langle f_1, f_2 \rangle : A_1 + A_2 \to B^*$ that applies $f_1$ or $f_2$ depending on
  the summand;
- *concatenation*: for $f_1 : A_1 \to B^*$ and $f_2 : A_2 \to B^*$, the term
  $f_1 \odot f_2 : A_1 \times A_2 \to B^*$ that maps $(a_1, a_2)$ to $f_1(a_1)\,f_2(a_2)$;
- *homomorphism*: for $f : A \to B^*$, the term $\mathrm{hom}\, f : A^* \to B^*$ that maps
  $[a_1, \ldots, a_n]$ to $f(a_1) \cdots f(a_n)$;
- *constants*: for $f : A \to B^*$ and a string $w \in B^*$, the terms $w \cdot f$ and
  $f \cdot w$, which prepend or append $w$ to the output.

A function is *represented* by a simple rational term if it is the function that the term
defines.

  | empty : SimpleTerm Bs Ty.unit
  /-- Co-pairing `⟨f₁, f₂⟩ : A₁ + A₂ → Bs*`. -/
  | either {A₁ A₂ : Ty} : SimpleTerm Bs A₁ → SimpleTerm Bs A₂ → SimpleTerm Bs (A₁ ⊕' A₂)
  /-- Concatenation `f₁ ⊙ f₂ : A₁ × A₂ → Bs*`. -/
  | conc {A₁ A₂ : Ty} : SimpleTerm Bs A₁ → SimpleTerm Bs A₂ → SimpleTerm Bs (A₁ ⊗ A₂)
  /-- Homomorphism `hom f : A* → Bs*`. -/
  | hom {A : Ty} : SimpleTerm Bs A → SimpleTerm Bs A⋆
  /-- Prepending a string constant, `w · f`. -/
  | pre {A : Ty} : List Bs → SimpleTerm Bs A → SimpleTerm Bs A
  /-- Appending a string constant, `f · w`. -/
  | post {A : Ty} : SimpleTerm Bs A → List Bs → SimpleTerm Bs A

namespace SimpleTerm

variable {Bs : Type}

/-- The function defined by a simple rational term. -/
def den : {A : Ty} → SimpleTerm Bs A → ⟦A⟧ → List Bs
  | _, .empty, _ => []
  | _, .either f _, .inl a => den f a
  | _, .either _ g, .inr b => den g b
  | _, .conc f g, (a, b) => den f a ++ den g b
  | _, .hom f, l => (l.map (den f)).flatten
  | _, .pre w f, a => w ++ den f a
  | _, .post f w, a => den f a ++ w

/-- A function is represented by a simple rational term if it is the function that the term
defines. -/
def IsSimpleFun {A : Ty} (f : ⟦A⟧ → List Bs) : Prop := ∃ t : SimpleTerm Bs A, t.den = f

end SimpleTerm

end Lax149335.SimpleRationalTerms

concepts.title: Simple rational terms within the compositional syntax
concepts.description:
The definition of simple rational terms (Definition 2.5) is meaningful in the compositional
syntax of Section 3: the *simple rational terms* with outputs in $B^*$ are the rational terms
built from the empty list $[\,] : 1 \to B^*$ using co-pairing $\langle f_1, f_2 \rangle$,
concatenation $f_1 \odot f_2$, the homomorphism combinator $\mathrm{hom}\, f$, and
prepending and appending a value, $w \cdot f$ and $f \cdot w$, where $w : 1 \to B^*$.

For two rational terms $f, g : A \to B^*$ and a value $w : 1 \to B^*$, Section 6 considers
three conjugacy relations, in increasing order of strength:

1. $f$ and $g$ are *denotationally $w$-conjugate* if
   $[\![ f \cdot w ]\!] = [\![ w \cdot g ]\!]$;
2. $f$ and $g$ are *provably $w$-conjugate* if $f \cdot w \equiv w \cdot g$;
3. $f$ and $g$ are *syntactically $w$-conjugate* if $f = w \cdot h$ and $g = h \cdot w$ for
   some term $h$.

The *length* of a list value $w$ is the length of the list it produces.

type: definition

syntax of Section 3: the *simple rational terms* with outputs in $B^*$ are the rational terms
built from the empty list $[\,] : 1 \to B^*$ using co-pairing $\langle f_1, f_2 \rangle$,

For two rational terms $f, g : A \to B^*$ and a value $w : 1 \to B^*$, Section 6 considers

1. $f$ and $g$ are *denotationally $w$-conjugate* if
   $[\![ f \cdot w ]\!] = [\![ w \cdot g ]\!]$;
2. $f$ and $g$ are *provably $w$-conjugate* if $f \cdot w \equiv w \cdot g$;
3. $f$ and $g$ are *syntactically $w$-conjugate* if $f = w \cdot h$ and $g = h \cdot w$ for
   some term $h$.

The *length* of a list value $w$ is the length of the list it produces.
-/

namespace Lax149335.SimpleRationalWithinSyntax

open Lax149335.Types Lax149335.Terms Lax149335.DerivedTerms Lax149335.DerivedTerms.Term
  Lax149335.EquationalTheory

/-- Simple rational terms with outputs in `B*`, within the syntax of rational terms. -/
inductive IsSimple (B : Ty) : {A : Ty} → Term A B⋆ → Prop
  /-- The empty function `[] : 1 → B*`. -/
  | nil : IsSimple B (nilT B)
  /-- Co-pairing. -/
  | either {A₁ A₂ : Ty} {f₁ : Term A₁ B⋆} {f₂ : Term A₂ B⋆} :
      IsSimple B f₁ → IsSimple B f₂ → IsSimple B (Term.either f₁ f₂)
  /-- Concatenation of two functions. -/
  | fdot {A₁ A₂ : Ty} {f₁ : Term A₁ B⋆} {f₂ : Term A₂ B⋆} :
      IsSimple B f₁ → IsSimple B f₂ → IsSimple B (f₁ ⊙ f₂)
  /-- The homomorphism combinator. -/
  | hom {A : Ty} {f : Term A B⋆} : IsSimple B f → IsSimple B (homT f)
  /-- Prepending a value. -/
  | dotL {A : Ty} {f : Term A B⋆} (w : Value B⋆) : IsSimple B f → IsSimple B (Term.dotL w f)
  /-- Appending a value. -/
  | dotR {A : Ty} {f : Term A B⋆} (w : Value B⋆) : IsSimple B f → IsSimple B (Term.dotR f w)

/-- The length of a list value. -/
def valLength {B : Ty} (w : Value B⋆) : ℕ := List.length (w.den ())

/-- `f` and `g` are denotationally `w`-conjugate: `⟦f · w⟧ = ⟦w · g⟧`. -/
def DenConjugate {A B : Ty} (w : Value B⋆) (f g : Term A B⋆) : Prop :=
  (dotR f w).den = (dotL w g).den

/-- `f` and `g` are provably `w`-conjugate: `f · w ≡ w · g`. -/
def ProvConjugate {A B : Ty} (w : Value B⋆) (f g : Term A B⋆) : Prop :=
  dotR f w ≡ₜ dotL w g

/-- `f` and `g` are syntactically `w`-conjugate: `f = w · h` and `g = h · w` for some `h`. -/
def SynConjugate {A B : Ty} (w : Value B⋆) (f g : Term A B⋆) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : Term A B⋆, f = dotL w h ∧ g = dotR h w

end Lax149335.SimpleRationalWithinSyntax

$$

namespace Lax149335.SynchronisedLengths

open Lax149335.Types Lax149335.SimpleRationalTerms

namespace SimpleTerm

variable {Bs : Type}

/-- The type `A₁* × (A₂* × ⋯ × (Aₙ* × 1))`. -/
def prodListTy : List Ty → Ty
  | [] => Ty.unit
  | A :: As => Ty.prod A⋆ (prodListTy As)

/-- A list of pairs `(fᵢ, wᵢ)` of a simple rational term `fᵢ : Aᵢ → Bs*` and a string `wᵢ`. -/
inductive HomList (Bs : Type) : List Ty → Type
  | nil : HomList Bs []
  | cons {A : Ty} {As : List Ty} : SimpleTerm Bs A → List Bs → HomList Bs As →
      HomList Bs (A :: As)

/-- The term `(hom f₁ · w₁) ⊙ ⋯ ⊙ (hom fₙ · wₙ)` of a list of pairs. -/
def HomList.term : {As : List Ty} → HomList Bs As → SimpleTerm Bs (prodListTy As)
  | _, .nil => .empty
  | _, .cons f w rest => .conc (.post (.hom f) w) rest.term

/-- Two lists of pairs whose terms `fᵢ` and `gᵢ` produce outputs of the same length on every
input. -/
def HomList.SameLengths : {As : List Ty} → HomList Bs As → HomList Bs As → Prop
  | _, .nil, .nil => True
  | _, .cons f _ F, .cons g _ G =>
      (∀ a, (f.den a).length = (g.den a).length) ∧ HomList.SameLengths F G

end SimpleTerm

open SimpleTerm

/-- **Claim 2.7.** If `w₀ · (hom f₁ · w₁) ⊙ ⋯ ⊙ (hom fₙ · wₙ)` and

outputs of the same length on every input. -/

    (SimpleRationalTerms.SimpleTerm.pre w₀ F.term).den =
      (SimpleRationalTerms.SimpleTerm.pre v₀ G.term).den →
    F.SameLengths G

end Lax149335.SynchronisedLengths

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax149335.Types
import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs

/-!
---
title: Rational terms
type: definition
---
**Definition 3.1 (Rational terms).** A *rational term* $f : A \to B$ between types is an
expression built from the following atomic functions (Figure 1) using composition
$f \mathbin{;} g$ and the functoriality combinators $f \times g$, $f + g$ and $f^*$ of
products, co-products and lists:

1. the identity $A \to A$;
2. the co-projections $\mathsf{Left} : A \to A + B$ and $\mathsf{Right} : B \to A + B$;
3. the co-diagonal $A + A \to A$;
4. the projections $\mathsf{fst} : A \times B \to A$ and $\mathsf{snd} : A \times B \to B$;
5. the units $A \to A \times 1$ and $A \to 1 \times A$, and associativity of products in
   both directions;
6. distributivity $A \times (B + C) \to A \times B + A \times C$ and
   $(A + B) \times C \to A \times C + B \times C$;
7. the list constructors and destructors $\mathsf{cons} : 1 + A \times A^* \to A^*$,
   $\mathsf{uncons}$, $\mathsf{snoc} : 1 + A^* \times A \to A^*$ and $\mathsf{unsnoc}$;
8. list concatenation $\mathsf{concat} : A^{**} \to A^*$;
9. $\mathsf{split} : (A + B)^* \to A^* \times (B \times A^*)^*$, which cuts a list before
   every element of $B$;
10. bracket shifting $\mathsf{shiftR} : (A \times B)^* \times A \to A \times (B \times A)^*$
    and its inverse $\mathsf{shiftL}$;
11. prefix multiplication $\mathsf{pref} : (A \times G)^* \to (A \times G)^*$ for a finite
    group $G$, which replaces the $i$-th group element by the product of the first $i$ ones.

The *denotation* $[\![ f ]\!]$ of a rational term is the function it defines. A rational
term is *aperiodic* if it does not use prefix multiplication.

# Formalization notes

A finite group is given by a group structure on a finite alphabet $\overline{n+1}$, which is
no loss of generality since every finite group is isomorphic to one of these.
-/

namespace Lax149335.Terms

open Lax149335.Types

/-- Auxiliary function used for the denotation of the group prefix multiplication: the `i`-th
group element of the output is the product of the first `i` group elements of the input. -/
def prefixMul {α G : Type} [Mul G] : G → List (α × G) → List (α × G)
  | _, [] => []
  | acc, (a, g) :: t => (a, acc * g) :: prefixMul (acc * g) t

/-- Auxiliary function used for the denotation of `split`: a list over `A + B` is split into a
maximal prefix of elements of `A`, followed by a list of blocks, each consisting of one
element of `B` and the following maximal run of elements of `A`. -/
def splitDen {α β : Type} : List (α ⊕ β) → List α × List (β × List α)
  | [] => ([], [])
  | .inl a :: t => let p := splitDen t; (a :: p.1, p.2)
  | .inr b :: t => let p := splitDen t; ([], (b, p.1) :: p.2)

/-- Auxiliary function used for the denotation of `snoc`. -/
def snocDen {α : Type} : Unit ⊕ (List α × α) → List α
  | .inl _ => []
  | .inr (l, a) => l ++ [a]

/-- Auxiliary function used for the denotation of `unsnoc`. -/
def unsnocDen {α : Type} (l : List α) : Unit ⊕ (List α × α) :=
  match l.reverse with
  | [] => .inl ()
  | a :: t => .inr (t.reverse, a)

/-- Auxiliary function used for the denotation of `shiftR`. -/
def shiftRDen {α β : Type} : List (α × β) → α → α × List (β × α)
  | [], a => (a, [])
  | (a₁, b₁) :: t, a => let p := shiftRDen t a; (a₁, (b₁, p.1) :: p.2)

/-- Auxiliary function used for the denotation of `shiftL`. -/
def shiftLDen {α β : Type} (a : α) : List (β × α) → List (α × β) × α
  | [] => ([], a)
  | (b₁, a₂) :: t => let p := shiftLDen a₂ t; ((a, b₁) :: p.1, p.2)

/-- **Definition 3.1 (Rational terms).** The expressions built from the atomic functions of
Figure 1 by composition and the functoriality combinators of products, co-products and
lists. -/
inductive Term : Ty → Ty → Type
  /-- Composition of functions. -/
  | comp {A B C : Ty} : Term A B → Term B C → Term A C
  /-- Functoriality of the product type constructor. -/
  | prodF {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ : Ty} : Term A₁ B₁ → Term A₂ B₂ → Term (A₁ ⊗ A₂) (B₁ ⊗ B₂)
  /-- Functoriality of the co-product type constructor. -/
  | sumF {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ : Ty} : Term A₁ B₁ → Term A₂ B₂ → Term (A₁ ⊕' A₂) (B₁ ⊕' B₂)
  /-- Functoriality of the list type constructor. -/
  | listF {A B : Ty} : Term A B → Term A⋆ B⋆
  /-- Atomic function 1: the identity. -/
  | id (A : Ty) : Term A A
  /-- Atomic function 2: the left co-projection. -/
  | inl (A B : Ty) : Term A (A ⊕' B)
  /-- Atomic function 2: the right co-projection. -/
  | inr (A B : Ty) : Term B (A ⊕' B)
  /-- Atomic function 3: the co-diagonal. -/
  | codiag (A : Ty) : Term (A ⊕' A) A
  /-- Atomic function 4: the first projection. -/
  | fst (A B : Ty) : Term (A ⊗ B) A
  /-- Atomic function 4: the second projection. -/
  | snd (A B : Ty) : Term (A ⊗ B) B
  /-- Atomic function 5: the right unit `(id, 1)`. -/
  | unitR (A : Ty) : Term A (A ⊗ Ty.unit)
  /-- Atomic function 5: the left unit `(1, id)`. -/
  | unitL (A : Ty) : Term A (Ty.unit ⊗ A)
  /-- Atomic function 5: left associativity of products. -/
  | assocL (A B C : Ty) : Term (A ⊗ (B ⊗ C)) ((A ⊗ B) ⊗ C)
  /-- Atomic function 5: right associativity of products. -/
  | assocR (A B C : Ty) : Term ((A ⊗ B) ⊗ C) (A ⊗ (B ⊗ C))
  /-- Atomic function 6: distributivity on the right. -/
  | distR (A B C : Ty) : Term (A ⊗ (B ⊕' C)) ((A ⊗ B) ⊕' (A ⊗ C))
  /-- Atomic function 6: distributivity on the left. -/
  | distL (A B C : Ty) : Term ((A ⊕' B) ⊗ C) ((A ⊗ C) ⊕' (B ⊗ C))
  /-- Atomic function 7: the list constructor `cons`. -/
  | cons (A : Ty) : Term (Ty.unit ⊕' (A ⊗ A⋆)) A⋆
  /-- Atomic function 7: the list destructor `uncons`. -/
  | uncons (A : Ty) : Term A⋆ (Ty.unit ⊕' (A ⊗ A⋆))
  /-- Atomic function 7: the list constructor `snoc`. -/
  | snoc (A : Ty) : Term (Ty.unit ⊕' (A⋆ ⊗ A)) A⋆
  /-- Atomic function 7: the list destructor `unsnoc`. -/
  | unsnoc (A : Ty) : Term A⋆ (Ty.unit ⊕' (A⋆ ⊗ A))
  /-- Atomic function 8: concatenation of a list of lists. -/
  | concat (A : Ty) : Term A⋆⋆ A⋆
  /-- Atomic function 9: splitting a list over a co-product. -/
  | split (A B : Ty) : Term (A ⊕' B)⋆ (A⋆ ⊗ (B ⊗ A⋆)⋆)
  /-- Atomic function 10: shifting brackets to the right. -/
  | shiftR (A B : Ty) : Term ((A ⊗ B)⋆ ⊗ A) (A ⊗ (B ⊗ A)⋆)
  /-- Atomic function 10: shifting brackets to the left. -/
  | shiftL (A B : Ty) : Term (A ⊗ (B ⊗ A)⋆) ((A ⊗ B)⋆ ⊗ A)
  /-- Atomic function 11: prefix multiplication in a finite group whose underlying set is the
  finite alphabet `1 + ⋯ + 1`. -/
  | pref (A : Ty) {n : ℕ} (G : Group ⟦Ty.finAlph n⟧) :
      Term ((A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n)⋆) ((A ⊗ Ty.finAlph n)⋆)

namespace Term

/-- Notation `f ⨟ g` for the composition of rational terms: first `f`, then `g`. -/
infixl:60 " ⨟ " => Term.comp

/-- The denotation `⟦f⟧` of a rational term: the function that it defines. -/
def den : {A B : Ty} → Term A B → ⟦A⟧ → ⟦B⟧
  | _, _, .comp f g, x => den g (den f x)
  | _, _, .prodF f g, x => (den f x.1, den g x.2)
  | _, _, .sumF f g, x =>
      match x with
      | .inl a => .inl (den f a)
      | .inr b => .inr (den g b)
  | _, _, .listF f, l => l.map (den f)
  | _, _, .id _, x => x
  | _, _, .inl _ _, x => .inl x
  | _, _, .inr _ _, x => .inr x
  | _, _, .codiag _, x => match x with | .inl a => a | .inr a => a
  | _, _, .fst _ _, x => x.1
  | _, _, .snd _ _, x => x.2
  | _, _, .unitR _, x => (x, ())
  | _, _, .unitL _, x => ((), x)
  | _, _, .assocL _ _ _, x => ((x.1, x.2.1), x.2.2)
  | _, _, .assocR _ _ _, x => (x.1.1, (x.1.2, x.2))
  | _, _, .distR _ _ _, x =>
      match x with
      | (a, .inl b) => .inl (a, b)
      | (a, .inr c) => .inr (a, c)
  | _, _, .distL _ _ _, x =>
      match x with
      | (.inl a, c) => .inl (a, c)
      | (.inr b, c) => .inr (b, c)
  | _, _, .cons _, x => match x with | .inl _ => [] | .inr (a, l) => a :: l
  | _, _, .uncons _, l => match l with | [] => .inl () | a :: t => .inr (a, t)
  | _, _, .snoc _, x => snocDen x
  | _, _, .unsnoc _, l => unsnocDen l
  | _, _, .concat _, l => l.flatten
  | _, _, .split _ _, l => splitDen l
  | _, _, .shiftR _ _, x => match x with | (l, a) => shiftRDen l a
  | _, _, .shiftL _ _, x => match x with | (a, l) => shiftLDen a l
  | _, _, .pref _ G, l => letI := G; prefixMul (1 : ⟦Ty.finAlph _⟧) l

/-- Whether a rational term uses the atomic function `pref` for prefix multiplication in
groups. -/
def usesPref : {A B : Ty} → Term A B → Bool
  | _, _, .comp f g => usesPref f || usesPref g
  | _, _, .prodF f g => usesPref f || usesPref g
  | _, _, .sumF f g => usesPref f || usesPref g
  | _, _, .listF f => usesPref f
  | _, _, .pref _ _ => true
  | _, _, _ => false

end Term

/-- A rational term is aperiodic if it does not use the group prefix multiplication `pref`. -/
def IsAperiodic {A B : Ty} (f : Term A B) : Prop := Term.usesPref f = false

end Lax149335.Terms

concepts.title: Types
concepts.description:
*Types* are the expressions generated by the grammar
$$
A \;::=\; 1 \;\mid\; A \times A \;\mid\; A + A \;\mid\; A^* .
$$
A type denotes a set: $1$ is a one-element set, $A \times B$ is the Cartesian product,
$A + B$ is the disjoint union, and $A^*$ is the set of finite lists over $A$.

Elements of types are represented as strings over the eight-letter alphabet
$$
\mathbb{8} = \{\, (\,,\ )\,,\ [\,,\ ]\,,\ \texttt{,}\,,\ 1,\ \mathsf{Left},\ \mathsf{Right} \,\}:
$$
the element of $1$ is written $1$, an element of $A + B$ is written $\mathsf{Left}\,a$ or
$\mathsf{Right}\,b$, a pair is written $(a,b)$ and a list is written $[a_1,\ldots,a_n]$.

A type is a *finite alphabet* if it has the form $1 + \cdots + 1$. We write
$\overline{n+1}$ for the finite alphabet with $n+1$ letters, bracketed to the right.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The finite alphabet with $n+1$ letters is `Ty.finAlph n`, defined as `1` for $n = 0$ and
as `1 + finAlph n` otherwise. A type is a finite alphabet (`Ty.IsFinAlph`) if it is equal
to one of these; the paper does not fix a bracketing of the sum, and any bracketing is
isomorphic to the right-bracketed one.

`Ty.someElem` picks a canonical element of every type; it shows that every type is
nonempty and is used to state the decision procedure of Corollary 2.8.
